text: During the whole of a dull, dark, and soundless autumn day. <break time="0.8s" /> I had been riding alone on horseback. <break time="0.8s" /> Through a dreary stretch of country. <break time="0.8s" /> At last as the evening shadows drew on I found myself. <break time="0.8s" /> Within view of the gloomy House of Usher. <break time="0.8s" /> The home of my old friend. <break time="0.8s" /> I do not know why. <break time="0.8s" /> But with the first glimpse of the building. <break time="0.8s" /> A feeling of unbearable gloom. <break time="0.8s" /> Filled my spirit. <break time="0.8s" /> I looked upon the bare walls. <break time="0.8s" /> The empty, eye like windows. <break time="0.8s" /> And a few white trunks of dead trees. <break time="0.8s" /> And my heart sank. <break time="0.8s" /> Hoping to change. <break time="0.8s" /> The sad effect of the scene. <break time="0.8s" /> I rode my horse. <break time="0.8s" /> To the edge of a black, silent tarn. <break time="0.8s" /> Beside the house. <break time="0.8s" /> But looking down. <break time="0.8s" /> At the upside down image of the house. <break time="0.8s" /> In the water. <break time="0.8s" /> I felt a shudder. <break time="0.8s" /> Even stronger than before. <break time="0.8s" /> Its owner, Roderick Usher. <break time="0.8s" /> Had been one of my closest companions. <break time="0.8s" /> In boyhood. <break time="0.8s" /> But many years had passed. <break time="0.8s" /> Since our last meeting. <break time="0.8s" /> Recently a letter had reached me. <break time="0.8s" /> From him. <break time="0.8s" /> In which he wrote. <break time="0.8s" /> Of an illness of body and mind. <break time="0.8s" /> And begged me to visit him. <break time="0.8s" /> Studying the house more closely. <break time="0.8s" /> I noticed a barely visible crack. <break time="0.8s" /> Which ran from the roof down the wall. <break time="0.8s" /> In a zigzag line. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the dark water.
